summary: For iid Uniform[0,1]^4 and A=I-J_4/8, whose eigenvalues are {1,1,1,1/2}, let v=(1,1,1,1)/2, Q3=||(I-vv^T)X||^2 and Q'=(v^TX)^2/2. With tau=4-sum_i X_i in (0,1), conditioning on Q'=b=(4-tau)^2/8 gives Q3=tau^2 T for a fixed nondegenerate T supported on [0,3/4]. Hence ||p_(Q3|Q'=b)||_infinity=tau^-2||p_T||_infinity>=4/(3tau^2), so the literal essential supremum over b is infinite. Meanwhile p_Q'(b)=tau^3/(3s), s=2-tau/2, and the weighted conditional contribution is tau/(3s) p_T(q/tau^2): the missing scalar-rest weight overcompensates the normalized peak. The full output density in this same example is bounded by 4sqrt(2)pi^2 via an ellipsoid-shell estimate. Thus the scalar-Q_rest conditional-supremum bridge is false, while QFORM itself is not refuted.
